expectations.text: Accepts streaming push only against the three named conditions: genuinely event-shaped data, consumer demand for sub-minute delivery, and consumer acceptance of the durability trade-off
expectations.evidence: The conditions listed are event-shaped, sub-minute demand, and '3-hour batch fails the use case'. Consumer acceptance of the durability trade-off is missing.

expectations.text: States explicitly that with a non-replayable stream a consumer whose endpoint was down recovers nothing from the provider
expectations.evidence: Braze Currents can't replay events, so a consumer outage means permanent loss.

expectations.text: Identifies streaming push as the highest-effort rung and the one that loses every efficiency comparison
expectations.evidence: The skill ranks streaming push last on effort and efficiency.

expectations.text: Recommends also shipping a file-drop or batch surface for historical backfill, which the stream cannot serve
expectations.evidence: hourly Parquet drop ... covers late data, lost events and ML backfills.

expectations.text: Notes that Avro, with schema-registry-based evolution, rather than Parquet, is the format used on the streaming rung
expectations.evidence: Uses a JSON envelope; Avro not mentioned.

expectations.text: Does not promise replay, at-least-once recovery or gap-filling unless a separate durable buffer is explicitly designed for it
expectations.evidence: Replay depends on the internal bus holding 7 days with time-range replay, flagged 'Verify before you publish the replay promise.'

expectations.text: Keeps the streaming surface gated behind a paid or enterprise contract rather than self-serve, consistent with the precedent in this feature class
